ai_metadata.description_ai: The seat of Mughal power for 200 years, this red sandstone fortress is a symbol of India's sovereignty and architectural brilliance.
The tallest brick minaret in the world, surrounded by complex ruins including the 4th-century uncorroded Iron Pillar.
The first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent, its Persian-style architecture served as the inspiration for the Taj Mahal.
A 42-meter high war memorial archway honors Indian soldiers; the surrounding Kartavya Path is Delhi's premier public space.
A Bahá'í House of Worship shaped like a floating lotus, open to people of all religions for silent meditation.
A massive spiritual complex showcasing millennia of traditional Indian and Hindu culture, spirituality, and architecture.
One of the oldest and busiest markets in India; a sensory explosion of spices, jewelry, and legendary Mughlai street food.
A sprawling 90-acre park containing the tombs of the Sayyid and Lodhi rulers amidst manicured greenery.
One of the largest mosques in India, built by Shah Jahan; its courtyard can hold 25,000 devotees.
A permanent open-air food and craft bazaar representing rural art and ethnic food from across India's states.
Established in 1913, this world-renowned restaurant is famous for its Mutton Korma and Burra Kebabs near Jama Masjid.
A unique theme park featuring replicas of the Seven Wonders of the World created entirely from industrial and scrap waste.
A massive circular commercial center defined by white colonial pillars, high-end brands, and some of the city's best bars.
A fusion of 14th-century Islamic architecture and modern urban culture, featuring upscale boutiques, lakeside cafes, and vibrant pubs.
One of India's largest museums, housing over 200,000 artifacts spanning 5,000 years, including the Harappan gallery and Buddhist relics.
A vibrant Tibetan colony famous for its monastery, authentic Himalayan cuisine (Mitho Mitho), and unique handicrafts shopping.
A major Sikh house of worship known for its holy pond (Sarovar) and massive community kitchen (Langar) that serves thousands daily.
A protected 60-meter long historical stepwell featuring 108 steps and unique niche architecture, popularized by Bollywood films.
Housed in the former palace of the Maharaja of Jaipur, it contains over 14,000 works of art including Raja Ravi Varma and Amrita Sher-Gil.
Delhi's most famous flea market known for export surplus clothes and trendy fashion at throwaway prices. Bargaining is mandatory here.
The mausoleum of Sufi saint Nizamuddin Auliya; famous for its soul-stirring evening Qawwali sessions and medieval atmosphere.
A 20-acre leisure space designed to stimulate the five senses through themed gardens, wind chimes, and stone murals.
A 176-acre zoo housing the famous White Tiger, Asiatic Lions, and diverse avian species near the Old Fort.
One of the oldest forts in Delhi, believed to be the site of the ancient city of Indraprastha from the Mahabharata.
Ranked as India's most expensive retail street, famous for its high-end boutiques, bookstores, and chic cafes.
A world-famous lane in Chandni Chowk serving deep-fried stuffed paranthas since the 1870s.
A simple black marble memorial marking the spot of Mahatma Gandhi's cremation, surrounded by lush lawns.
An open-air museum designed as a village, showcasing diverse Indian textiles, terracotta, and folk art.
The last monumental garden tomb of the Mughal era, often called the 'Last Flicker of Mughal Architecture'.
A restored 16th-century heritage park containing 15 monuments and over 300 tree species; Delhi's answer to Central Park.
A sprawling museum showcasing the exotic heritage of Indian Railways, featuring the Fairy Queen steam engine and royal saloons.
A world-famous backpacker ghetto known for its cheap hotels, international cafes, and a market selling everything from incense to leather goods.
One of the largest science centers in Asia, featuring hands-on exhibits, a 3D theater, and galleries on nuclear power and pre-historic life.
Famous for the Tibetan Market and street stalls selling silver jewelry, ethnic wear, and brass decorative items.
A monument dedicated to the Indian Armed Forces, featuring concentric circles and a central obelisk with an eternal flame.
One of the largest temple complexes in India, featuring a 'Vedic Cultural Centre' and a magnificent robot-assisted show on the Gita.
Includes stops like Old Famous Jalebi Wala and Natraj Dahi Bhalle. A journey through the culinary heart of Mughal India.
